title: Myth flip — perimenopause starts at 3am, not with hot flashes (Rita, 44)
caption:
Myth: menopause starts with hot flashes. Often it starts with 3am anxiety, years earlier. Cycle-length change stages it, not one FSH test (STRAW+10).
Send this to whoever's up at 3am. Which myth next? 👇
www.aiforheratx.org
#perimenopause #menopause #womenshealth #perimenopausesupport #midlifewomen

scenes.text: "I'm too young for menopause." So why *awake* at 3am, again?

scenes.text: Everyone had a theory about her sleep. Nobody asked about her *cycles*.
phrases: You're way too young for that.
It's been a year of 3am. I'm not stressed, I'm *scared* something's wrong.

scenes.text: Hot flashes weren't the first sign. Her *cycles* changed first — 28 days, then 40.
phrases: Hot flashes weren't first for her.
Her periods went 28 days, then 40, then 26.
A repeated 7+ day swing between cycles is what marks the early transition (STRAW+10, 2012).

scenes.text: Depression risk roughly doubles in the transition, even with no history of it. Mood is a *symptom*.

scenes.text: Log every period start date, and ask about *CBT* — it's a real non-hormonal option.
phrases: Notes app: the date every period starts.
Two cycles 7+ days apart is data your doctor can actually use.
Ask about CBT for the sleep and flashes — it's evidence-based, not fluff.
And 150 minutes of walking a week (WHO) helps the sleep too.
